verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas makes its APIs very LLM-friendly. It serves llms.txt plus a roughly 2MB llms-full.txt of complete docs, and new projects ship PlayCanvas Skills that give AI coding agents development and verification workflows. It also offers 12 runnable create-playcanvas starters and a long-lived open-source MIT engine on npm with about 48k weekly downloads, a reasonable proxy for public examples models may have seen. However, nothing shows LLM-generated code actually working on the first try. API stability is also not demonstrated: the move to ESM scripts recommended for new projects implies two scripting styles, and community comments describe dev-experience friction and ongoing ES module and TypeScript transitions. missing for 10: hands-on evidence of LLM first-try success rates, documented API stability/deprecation policy, evidence of example abundance in the wild (e.g., third-party tutorials or volume compared with peers)
